title: Five of the seven previously flagged findings are resolved; two scope risks remain, with no new numerical error identified.

items.location: main.md:11–14 — Abstract: scope of the rule
items.old: the statistical rule of three governs what missing fossils can say
items.new: the rule of three applies: with finding level after the oldest fossil
items.problem: Resolved in context. The later plateau is now explicit, and “fits” describes compatibility. The Conditions paragraph supplies the count-derived scaling, cutoff and treatment of delay.
items.evidence: C58 restricts this to the conditional body-record calculation. Methods (g) distinguishes compatibility for retrospective histories from confidence coverage.

items.location: main.md:15–20 — Abstract: numerical summary and proxies
items.old: 431.2 Ma if about half are; less non-marine rock and fewer trilete-reporting studies match the requirements
items.new: near 431.2 Ma if about half are; North American non-marine rock area and trilete-reporting shares ... matching some requirements
items.problem: Partly resolved. “Near 431.2” correctly describes the half-count result, and reporting shares replace study counts. However, the delay branch still needs its steady-rate condition. “Rock area” also obscures column area, “North American” can appear to qualify both proxies, and “matching” should explicitly mean numerical overlap.
items.evidence: At n=24 the bound is 431.1178 Ma; the exact crossing is n=23.588. C33's minimum delays assume steady finding. C56 concerns North American column area and a global document reporting share, with proportional transfer untested.
items.repair: Use “or, at a steady finding rate with all 48 finds independent, if recognisable bodies appeared at least about 15–23 Myr later”. Then: “North American non-marine column-area ratios and global trilete-reporting-share ratios overlap some requirements numerically; their transfer to body-fossil finding remains untested.”

items.old: p=K/(A-c+K), and no early find has probability (1-p)^n=0.05
items.new: p=R/(A-c+R); at the boundary R=K, no early find has probability (1-p)^n=0.05
items.problem: Resolved. The probability now uses actual earlier exposure, with equality restricted to the boundary.
items.evidence: The stated transformation gives m*=n(0.05^(-1/n)-1), agreeing with C58 and rule_of_three.csv. The rule-of-three approximation is correctly distinguished from that exact expression.

items.location: main.md:228–256 — Results (d): scope of the opening rule
items.old: One rule underlies every body-fossil result that follows
items.new: One rule underlies the results that follow, which hold the finding rate level after the oldest find
items.problem: Partly resolved. Expected counts and count-derived rate estimation are now clear. But the scope statement remains false: this same subsection subsequently reports collection-dependent and exponentially declining later rates, plus shape tests.
items.evidence: Lines 249–256 discuss histories without the common later plateau. C58's rule does not subsume those later-age shape diagnostics.
items.repair: Replace the opening with: “The calculations with a level finding rate after the oldest find share one compatibility rule.”

items.old: leaving the 2.1 Myr that three finds take
items.new: leaving at most the 2.1 Myr that three finds take
items.problem: Resolved. “At most” now covers delays longer than the minimum.
items.evidence: C33 and rule_of_three.csv give minimum delays of 15.1600 and 23.1600 Myr. Equality leaves 2.1400 Myr before the oldest find; longer delays leave less.

items.old: finding scaled down by the rock measure would still have yielded about 8–11 finds
items.new: if body-fossil finding were proportional to each measure in both windows ... finds would have been expected
items.problem: Resolved. Both the counterfactual proportionality and expected-count interpretation are explicit.
items.evidence: rule_of_three.csv gives rock expectations 7.5861–11.4602 and spore-share expectations 4.8615–5.1437, all above m*(48)=3.0912. The Conditions paragraph specifies the same proportionality constant in both windows.

items.location: main.md:399–409 — Conclusion: body record, proxies and Libyan supply
items.old: allows about three missed finds; trilete supply there stayed below about a tenth
items.new: about three expected finds; steady trilete supply since 459.1 Ma ... with older onsets needing less
items.problem: Resolved. The Conclusion restores expected counts, the later plateau, numerical proxy comparison with untested transfer, and the Libyan steady-supply history and onset. The alternatives of producers elsewhere or later acquisition of triletes preserve the distinction between ancestral presence and local spore supply.
items.evidence:
C24 gives 0.091 for equal-delivery steady supply from 459.1 Ma. The primary m2_results.csv row gives 0.0719 at 464 Ma and 0.058 at 469.4 Ma, supporting “older onsets needing less”. These conclusions were checked against current files. No files were edited.

Next: Claude — address the two remaining scope risks.
